answer.rationale: Primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line is at 94% and has no buffer, so deferral or a failed negotiation would cut supply and raise delivery risk. Incumbent already refused a price reopen, so negotiate_terms would spend the only decision on an ask they rejected. Switch or second-source would replace the expiring primary under time pressure; c1 is the only record that kept integration and deliveries intact. Renewing therefore meets the no-added-delivery-risk constraint; the 18% spend cut is unmet. Verifying c2 (whether a low-cost switch was truly low-risk on a short fuse) and c6 (whether a multi-year/volume structure could cut unit cost without leaving the incumbent). Not treating this as the non-critical month-to-month case in c5.
